title: Quarter Bridge: tiered fallback lanes for hosted API + model catalog
creator: Sana Patel
description: Create a compact, operable playbook for the quarter-bridge (inter-quarter) window that defines tiered fallback lanes for Hosted API routes and associated model catalog substitutions. Purpose: keep customer-facing endpoints within latency and cost SLOs during expected seasonal surges and model rotations while minimizing manual runbook intervention. Deliverables: (1) lane definitions (Green/Amber/Red) with concrete autoscale and fallback policies, (2) canary schedule and rollback triggers for model swaps, (3) simulation test harness and dashboards for validation, (4) rollout SOP and stakeholder sign-off checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Lane definitions published to the Console playbook page and included in runtime route policy templates
Automated fallback implemented for at least two high-traffic routes: chat.conversation and text.generate (fallback to quantized-compatible variants)
Canary rollout automation completes a 72-hour canary with automated alerting on regression signals (latency or output-quality) and documented rollback threshold
Capacity simulation runs complete with 3 scenarios (baseline, 2x surge, burst) and dashboards show expected autoscale headroom >= 20% for Green lane
Customer-facing SLA dashboard updated to show per-route 95th and 99th latency SLOs and cost delta for fallback activation
comments: 2026-02-11 Sana Patel: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded. Agreed scope: start with hosted chat and embed routes, iterate to other routes if successful.
2026-02-18 Owen Martinez: Draft lane thresholds posted. Proposal: Green = normal (<70% utilization), Amber = sustained 70-90%, Red = sustained >90% or persistent cache miss rate >50%.
2026-02-22 Dalia Chen (Eng): Requested that autoscale buffer be a config per-customer and default to 20% for Green. Also asked for a simulated 600k requests/day load test before sign-off.
2026-02-28 Miguel Rivera (Design): UX copy for Console lane selector and canary status card reviewed. Minor copy edits scheduled.
2026-03-03 Owen Martinez: Implemented canary window automation prototype. Canary fraction defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 72h with regression stop if quality score drops >3 points.
2026-03-10 QA: Smoke tests passed for fallback on chat.conversation route; found edge case when prompt length >2048 tokens causing fallback to be ineffective — added follow-up ENG task.
2026-03-12 Sana Patel: Stakeholder review completed. PM sign-off pending runtime perf numbers from ENG-2411.
Action items: ENG to complete perf run (ENG-2411), Growth to advise on canary customer cohorts, Support to prepare incident comms template.
decisions: Adopt tiered lane model (Green/Amber/Red) rather than per-route static thresholds to reduce ops overhead
Fallback strategy: prefer model-variant substitution (quantized or smaller architecture) over region reroute to minimize cross-region latency impact
Canary window set at 72 hours with progressive ramp fractions and automated stop conditions on both perf and quality signals
risk_mitigation: Add synthetic regression tests tied to a prompt-set representative of high-value customers to detect quality drift during canary
Temporarily pin high-risk customers to dedicated capacity if their traffic is expected to cause repeated Red-lane activations
Create automated alerting for unexpected cost delta > 15% after fallback activation and tie to on-call escalation policy
notes: Trade-offs discussed: more aggressive fallback reduces cost but risks quality; elected to keep conservative thresholds for first quarter run
We will instrument token-level cost attribution to evaluate real $/k-token impact of lane activations for OKR reporting
Plan to include a short tabletop incident drill in Q2 cycle to validate communication and rollback steps
